target_customer: Home coffee drinkers who buy specialty beans on subscription
problem: Coffee subscriptions ship on fixed schedules, so customers run out or pile up stock; usage based reordering fixes the timing.
business_model: subscription with a Wi-Fi scale included; membership $7.99 per month per the site, coffee bought from partner roasters

founders.name: Liana Herrera
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; a search snippet describes her and Mayer as a Seattle married couple, not verified by an opened source.

founders.name: Michael Mayer
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. A search snippet says he was a Nike.com developer; not confirmed by an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: A connected scale with firmware, an app and reorder logic across partner roasters is hardware plus software, but uses off the shelf components.

defensibility.rationale: The scale locks in a subscriber and tracks usage data, but coffee subscriptions are easy to copy and roasters are partners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying the scale model.

market_need_then: Product Hunt launch dated 2019-02-22 and a 2019 $1.9M raise show early interest; later coverage cites about 6,000 customers at the 2021 round (Preqin summary).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and helpful; the site uses sample customer profiles and 7 day support

branding.brand_signature: The smart scale under the coffee bag
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch and GeekWire and TechCrunch coverage; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests unlimited refills and fits the product, but no source shows meaningful brand pull beyond tech press.

outcome_analysis: Bottomless joined YC Winter 2019 after starting in 2016 as a side project. It raised $1.9M in 2019 and a $4.5M Series A in March 2021 from Positive Sum, Craft Ventures and others, and scaled customers through the pandemic. The company remains listed active with a two person YC team and no reported layoffs or sale, but there is no public data on retention or unit economics.
notes: GeekWire pages could not be fetched (domain check rate limited), so round figures come from search result text: the 2019 raise was reported as a $1.9M SEC filing and the 2021 Series A as $4.5M, with TechCrunch dated 2021-03-03 and another summary saying January 2021. Totals vary by aggregator ($6.4M, $6.8M, $9M). Competitors: no dated 2019 rival with a source was found. Founder prior employers and education not confirmed.
